UAT: **focused-test-pass-1**

`nheroux-bit` cannot apply labels on this repo (`AddLabelsToLabelable` denied). Please add the `focused-test-pass-1` label to this issue.
UAT Tester 6 hit the same class of problem on cold-start (doctor/init noise, unclear next step). Fresh write-up with WSL/Grok evidence: #4701

Adoption blocker.

This is about Lifecycle: installing Directive, updating it, and getting one clear next step when something looks wrong. It also covers whether the version someone thinks they installed is the version that is actually running.

What a new person hits: The first setup command succeeds, then prints a long maintainer log and several different things to do next.

Why that ruins the product for them: The first screen feels like the tool is bloated and aimed at its own developers. A new person cannot tell which line is for them.

How likely: High. Almost everyone who runs setup sees this output.

## sharpens-framing Creation lines already print

The recorded target says first-run success prints a maintainer git-add recipe and several next actions, rather than what was created and one next step. The recipe and the several next actions do print. What was created also prints, on that same success path.

Evidence. Pinned read of eec15b57b142591c99bd8a68c13dda573f1c03aa. Init was not executed.

printNextSteps in packages/core/src/init-deposit/init-deposit.ts lines 226-242 prints the success banner, then Location, AGENTS.md updated, Skills, and User config, then a Next steps list of four items, then printMigrateNudgeIfNeeded. runInitDepositCli calls that function on success (same file, lines 414 and 416).

runInitDeposit writes the VERSION manifest without managedBy (same file, lines 320-328). buildInstallManifestText adds managed_by only when that field is set (packages/core/src/init-deposit/scaffold.ts lines 154-157). shouldEmitMigrateNudge returns true when the manifest exists and is not npm-managed (packages/core/src/init-deposit/migrate.ts lines 456-468). A fresh init therefore prints the directive migrate line. The test at packages/core/src/init-deposit/init-deposit.test.ts lines 389-404 locks that same predicate on a hand-built non-npm manifest.

printCommitGuidance in packages/core/src/init-deposit/hygiene.ts lines 1463-1516 prints the upgrade recipe whenever the path list is nonempty. The commit-hygiene header, the git add -A warning, and the co-travel paragraph print first. The staging branch then prints one of the git-add sentences. The five-step chore/deft-framework-upgrade list (branch, commit, push, PR, merge) follows that branch, so it prints for every nonempty path list. runInitDeposit calls printCommitGuidance(io, stagePaths, staged) at init-deposit.ts lines 361-364. The cachedNames parameter defaults to an empty list (hygiene.ts line 1468). depositStagePaths already computed cachedNames, and this call drops it. hygiene.test.ts lines 1263-1266 lock the empty-cache branch to the Stage ONLY these sentence. The update path passes cachedNames (packages/core/src/init-deposit/refresh.ts lines 1106-1112) and calls this printer only when the deposit is not already current.

frameworkStagePaths adds .deft/core when the deposit directory exists (hygiene.ts lines 1025-1032). That directory exists before the guidance call, because reconstitute runs at init-deposit.ts line 313. Greenfield gitignore includes .deft/core/ when the deposit is not tracked (gitignore.ts lines 207-216; the line text is .deft/core/ at gitignore.ts line 31). A repository with no commits is that case: isDepositTrackedInGit is false when ls-files is empty. The printed git add uses the unfiltered stage list. stageFrameworkPaths drops untracked ignored paths before the real git add (hygiene.ts lines 1135-1137). No commit count gates the recipe.

Failure mode. Adding a creation summary repeats printNextSteps lines 228-232. Shortening only the Next steps list leaves the upgrade recipe on the path, because runInitDeposit prints it first. Passing cachedNames changes the git-add sentence. The five-step upgrade list still prints, because those lines follow the staging branch.

Disposition. Bind this statement: first-run success prints the maintainer git-add recipe and more than one next action, and it already names what was created. The edit stops the init success path from using the upgrade recipe, and leaves one next step from the list printNextSteps already prints. The absence wording in the recorded target stays out of the bound statement.

Road not taken. Blocking the whole sentence. The case for a block is that the absence wording makes the sentence unusable as a problem statement. The creation lines on this success path flip that to a scope change: the recipe half and the several-actions half can bind once that wording is dropped.

Comment 5781933530 cites relief for P1. Stop 1 write-back 5781763680 defines P1 as first-run init success output that names several next actions and a maintainer git-add recipe instead of one next step. The harvested edit stops the upgrade recipe and leaves one next step from the list printNextSteps already prints. That list is the four numbered items. The migrate nudge is the next call in the same function, and the harvested edit leaves that call in place.

Evidence. Pin-read with git show eec15b57b142591c99bd8a68c13dda573f1c03aa of the success-path printers. Init was not executed. This is the same method as the round-1 pin-read: follow the printers the success path calls.

printNextSteps in packages/core/src/init-deposit/init-deposit.ts lines 233-240 prints the Next steps heading and items 1 through 4. Line 241 calls printMigrateNudgeIfNeeded. runInitDeposit writes the VERSION manifest with no managedBy field (same file, lines 320-328). buildInstallManifestText appends managed_by only when that field is set (packages/core/src/init-deposit/scaffold.ts lines 154-157). shouldEmitMigrateNudge returns true when that manifest exists and is not npm-managed (packages/core/src/init-deposit/migrate.ts lines 456-468). The printed line tells the user to run directive migrate (migrate.ts lines 452-453). The test at packages/core/src/init-deposit/init-deposit.test.ts lines 389-404 locks that line on a non-npm manifest. Stop 1 cited that test under the P1 gate stamp. runInitDeposit calls printCommitGuidance at init-deposit.ts line 364, and runInitDepositCli calls printNextSteps on success (lines 414 and 416).

Failure mode. An implementer who follows the harvested edit removes the upgrade-recipe printer and keeps one of the four numbered steps. The nudge still prints on a fresh init, because the manifest that runInitDeposit writes has no managedBy. The success path then names that kept step and the migrate command. P1 asks for one next step. The relief cite does not cover P1.

Disposition. This lean cannot bind as written. The relief cite stays an asserted premise the harvested edit does not discharge.

## footnote Git-add sentence sits inside the stopped printer

Under the method comment 5781892529 recorded, and that this lean accepted, the upgrade recipe is printCommitGuidance (packages/core/src/init-deposit/hygiene.ts lines 1463-1516). That function prints the git add -- sentence (lines 1504-1506) and then the five-step upgrade list (lines 1508-1516). Stopping that printer removes the git-add recipe P1 names. A cut that stops only the five-step list would be a different method. This footnote is census only. It carries no disposition.

Road not taken. Treating the surviving nudge as a wording change and rewriting the edit so it also stops printMigrateNudgeIfNeeded. The case for that class is that the parent meant a single user-facing step and would accept the extra stop. The recorded edit leaves the nudge call in place, so the relief cite is false on the harvest that is posted. What would flip this verdict to a wording change: the bound edit already stops that nudge, or it defines the one remaining step as the only imperative the success path prints.

metadata.issueBody:
## Tester 1 (Codex / Windows / @deftai/directive@0.119.1)

**Checks:** C3 PASS letter / UX fail; C4 related
**Defect:** 3

### Expected
First-run success names what was created and gives one next step a new user can follow.

### What happened
Init dumped a maintainer upgrade-PR `git add` recipe (on a repo with **zero commits**), a JSON blob, a wall of LFâ†’CRLF warnings, hook fail-closed vs `ready: true`, `directive migrate`, "Use AGENTS.md" vs README `read AGENTS.md and follow it`, and `git add .deft/core` after saying `.deft/core` is gitignored.

### Evidence
Full `directive.cmd init` transcript from Tester 1. Coworker independently called it a blurb that does not make sense.

### Environment
Directive 0.119.1. Empty repo, no commits yet.
